
{{alias}}( N, k, order, x, strideX )
    Partitions a strided array using quickselect.

    The `N` and stride parameters determine which elements in the strided array
    are accessed at runtime.

    Indexing is relative to the first index. To introduce an offset, use typed
    array views.

    If `N <= 0`, `k < 0`, `k >= N`, or `order == 0`, the function returns `x`
    unchanged.

    Upon completion, the element at index `k` is the element which would be at
    that index were the strided array fully sorted according to `order`. When
    partitioned in increasing order, all elements preceding index `k` are less
    than or equal to the element at index `k`, and all elements following index
    `k` are greater than or equal to the element at index `k`. When partitioned
    in decreasing order, all elements preceding index `k` are greater than or
    equal to the element at index `k`, and all elements following index `k` are
    less than or equal to the element at index `k`. No other guarantees are
    made regarding the order of the elements preceding and following index `k`.

    The algorithm distinguishes between `-0` and `+0`, such that `-0` is
    considered less than `+0`.

    The algorithm considers `NaN` values to be greater than all other values.
    When partitioned in increasing order, `NaN` values are placed last. When
    partitioned in decreasing order, `NaN` values are placed first.

    The algorithm has space complexity O(1), average time complexity O(N), and
    worst case time complexity O(N^2).

    The input strided array is partitioned *in-place* (i.e., the input strided
    array is *mutated*).

    Parameters
    ----------
    N: integer
        Number of indexed elements.

    k: integer
        Partition index.

    order: number
        Sort order. If `order < 0`, the function partitions `x` in decreasing
        order. If `order > 0`, the function partitions `x` in increasing order.

    x: ArrayLikeObject
        Input array.

    strideX: integer
        Stride length.

    Returns
    -------
    x: ArrayLikeObject
        Input array.

    Examples
    --------
    // Standard Usage:
    > var x = [ 1.0, -2.0, 3.0, -4.0 ];
    > {{alias}}( x.length, 1, 1, x, 1 )
    [ -4.0, -2.0, 3.0, 1.0 ]

    // Using `N` and stride parameters:
    > x = [ 1.0, -2.0, 3.0, -4.0 ];
    > {{alias}}( 2, 0, -1, x, 2 )
    [ 3.0, -2.0, 1.0, -4.0 ]

    // Using view offsets:
    > var x0 = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 1.0, -2.0, 3.0, -4.0 ] );
    > var x1 = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( x0.buffer, x0.BYTES_PER_ELEMENT*1 );
    > {{alias}}( 2, 0, 1, x1, 2 )
    <Float64Array>[ -4.0, 3.0, -2.0 ]
    > x0
    <Float64Array>[ 1.0, -4.0, 3.0, -2.0 ]


{{alias}}.ndarray( N, k, order, x, strideX, offsetX )
    Partitions a strided array using quickselect and alternative indexing
    semantics.

    While typed array views mandate a view offset based on the underlying
    buffer, the offset parameter supports indexing semantics based on a starting
    index.

    Parameters
    ----------
    N: integer
        Number of indexed elements.

    k: integer
        Partition index.

    order: number
        Sort order. If `order < 0`, the function partitions `x` in decreasing
        order. If `order > 0`, the function partitions `x` in increasing order.

    x: ArrayLikeObject
        Input array.

    strideX: integer
        Stride length.

    offsetX: integer
        Starting index.

    Returns
    -------
    x: ArrayLikeObject
        Input array.

    Examples
    --------
    // Standard Usage:
    > var x = [ 1.0, -2.0, 3.0, -4.0 ];
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( x.length, 1, 1, x, 1, 0 )
    [ -4.0, -2.0, 3.0, 1.0 ]

    // Using an index offset:
    > x = [ 1.0, -2.0, 3.0, -4.0 ];
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( 2, 0, 1, x, 2, 1 )
    [ 1.0, -4.0, 3.0, -2.0 ]

    See Also
    --------
